content.value_statement: Compound triage needs consistent medicinal chemistry filters across large molecule sets. This skill guides Medchem workflows for rules, alerts, constraints, and batch reports.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to apply Lipinski, Veber, REOS, CNS, leadlike, and related rules.
Shows Medchem API patterns for rule filters, structural alerts, constraints, groups, catalogs, and complexity metrics.
Includes a batch filtering script for CSV, TSV, SDF, and text molecule inputs.
Combines selected filter outputs into CSV results and optional summary reports.
Points users to local API and rules references for parameters, thresholds, and caveats.
limitations: Requires Python dependencies such as medchem, datamol, pandas, RDKit, and tqdm.
Does not replace medicinal chemistry review or biological assay validation.
Filter results depend on input molecule quality and correct SMILES or SDF parsing.
Large libraries may need compute resources and careful n_jobs settings.

use_cases.title: Triage a screening library
use_cases.description: Apply drug-likeness rules and structural alerts before selecting compounds for experimental follow-up.

use_cases.title: Build a filtering pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan CSV or SDF batch processing with selected Medchem filters and reproducible output reports.

use_cases.title: Review lead optimization candidates
use_cases.description: Compare candidate molecules against stricter property constraints, alert filters, and complexity guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Screen a small molecule list
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Medchem skill to choose basic drug-likeness and alert filters for these SMILES. Explain each filter and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a batch filtering run
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Medchem workflow for a CSV file with a smiles column. Include rule filters, structural alerts, output columns, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare optimization criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend Medchem rules, constraints, and complexity thresholds for a lead optimization set. Explain tradeoffs and when to relax filters.

prompt_templates.title: Design a screening protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reproducible Medchem protocol for a 50,000 compound library. Cover dependencies, input checks, parallelization, result review, and reporting.

output_examples.input: A chemist asks whether aspirin-like molecules should pass basic drug-likeness triage.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Rule of Five and Veber checks, explains expected pass fields, and flags PAINS review as a follow-up.

output_examples.input: A data scientist has a vendor compound CSV and wants a filtering plan.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines input requirements, selected Medchem filters, result columns, and a summary report for pass rates.

output_examples.input: A lead optimization team wants stricter property limits for CNS candidates.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes CNS, TPSA, logP, rotatable bond, alert, and complexity checks with target-specific exception notes.

best_practices: Validate input structures before applying filters.
Combine rules with expert review and project context.
Record chosen filters, thresholds, and reasons for reproducibility.
anti_patterns: Treating filter pass status as proof of efficacy or safety.
Applying every filter without considering the target and chemical series.
Running large jobs without checking dependencies, input columns, and output locations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and explain Medchem filtering workflows for compound libraries and medicinal chemistry review.

faq.question: Does it install Medchem automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users choose when to install dependencies.

faq.question: Can it replace cheminformatics validation?
faq.answer: No. It supports triage and documentation, but expert review and assay validation remain necessary.

faq.question: What file types does the batch script support?
faq.answer: The script supports CSV, TSV, SDF, and text files with one SMILES string per line.

faq.question: Does it support PAINS and structural alerts?
faq.answer: Yes. The references and examples cover PAINS, common alerts, NIBR filters, and Lilly demerits.

faq.question: Can it handle large libraries?
faq.answer: Yes, Medchem supports parallel options such as n_jobs. Large runs still need enough memory and CPU.
